[2021-04-05 20:56] furysk : the idea on redshirting is also that you extend the time until that scholarship comes open again.
[2021-04-05 20:57] furysk : so basically, you have 5 seasons of 135 contacts if you redshirt all, versus 4 season of 135 contacts if you redshirt none
[2021-04-05 20:59] furysk : so 675 contacts to spend to get 13 scholarship players if all redshirt, or if you don't 540.
[2021-04-05 20:59] furysk : that doesn't mean you should see merits in redshirting all players because of that, just that you should probably plan to get at minimum 1/2 the lineup redshirted before the graduate
[2021-04-05 20:59] furysk : because you also don't have them active for 1 of those 5
[2021-04-05 20:59] furysk : this is directed to rupascoop
[2021-04-05 21:00] furysk : you can pick and choose who to redshirt in the FR vs SO seasons, or even redshirt a JUCO as a JR.

[2021-04-21 19:33] bridger29 : "running some projections" sounds fancier than it is.  I just project a final build based on growth rate, starting skill values, and current skill values.  It's not a perfect science, but gives some idea of where a player might end up.  For example, my spreadsheet yields the following final build (I capped him at 189 SI even though he projects higher because that's the middle of 13-POT):  6'5.5" 205 lbs 83" Wing 35" Leap  15 IS 11 OS 18 RG 8 FN  11 RB 11 ID 15 PD  16 IQ 17 PA 15 BH 16 DV  12 STR 15 SPD 9 STA  I would prefer to play a player like that at SF because it's hard to find guys who can play outside and inside well...but the PG skills are all 15+, so if I need him at that spot, that's where he'll end up because PG is too important.  I'm sure that's way more information than anyone wanted!

[2021-04-21 21:16] bridger29 : It's not a big trade secret.  If a player had 48 SI at the start of high school and 88 SI at the end of high school, then they grew an average of 10 SI per year.  That means that with 5 years of college they project to 138 SI assuming growth rate stays steady (it doesn't, but it serves well enough for a projection).
[2021-04-21 21:16] bridger29 : From there, you basically just do the same math for each skill as a proportion of the total growth.
[2021-04-21 21:17] bridger29 : I am sure other people track much more complicated things and dig for data, but what I'm doing is nothing all that special!
[2021-04-21 21:27] bergkamp7349 : i dont even project player SIs or how they'll look in X years specifically - but if I know I have 2 non shooters, I won't recruit any more in the next few cycles. If I had two bad defenders I won't recruit another one of those...I'm about the general player build, and what position/s I need them to play then fill in behind them with your next class.   My actual HW spreadsheet has 1 tab for each team, which includes all the stuff on the HW roster page + growth per year, and their scouting reports. A little tab of which year each player will graduate + how many I need to recruit that season - i tend to note next to that what position / player build I need. Below there = depth charts for future seasons.  Graduated players I keep near the bottom of the sheet somewhere.   One tab for opponents, which for Lincoln I properly map out at the start of the year, SIs and position for each opposition player and then some kind of projection of strongest to weakest (I've done it for Knox as well, just not this season as I know I won't be competitive)  One recruiting tab, which I don't always use in depth but to compare a whole recruiting class and pick out your targets and backups it can be useful when I need somewhere to note this stuff.   One tab projecting Westfield's opponents for the next couple of seasons (working out when I should target for promotion...) that's not worth doing once you're above d6 as theres so much conference movement between seasons.   I had one Hall of Fame tab / historical player stat totals for Lincoln as well, but since then Steve has added this to HW so its no longer used   I don't do anything special really...

TIER - (S) - Main Star/s of the Team,  Face of the program, Guys you know that you want when they hit their Senior Year.  Guys that you think will carry you to what your goal is. TIER - (A) - Usually 3 Star Recruits (can also be 2 stars) that has really good current SI and potential. TIER - (B) - Provides quality minutes, Mono skilled Guys that will just play their role going in. I like to call them Hit mans. Just do their job then done see you next game. TIER - (C) - Projects (Not always required to get one) But could be a Tier B to A- type of player when he gets into red shirted senior year. Could be really useful.

[2021-05-15 02:17] pbyrnesomisssunycortland : Biggest recruiting challenge for a D2 team (at least for me) is recruiting good talent with limited (D2) recruiting fire power that will not only get you promoted to IV, but will also keep you up there once you're promoted. Andrew <@!711316787471581294> mentioned this on an earlier TPI podcast. It's not difficult to build a D2 team that promotes - the real challenge is recruiting a D2 roster that can "stick" once promoted to IV. That's what I'm struggling with right now.
[2021-05-15 02:35] cdilks : Consistency in recruiting is the key, I think. Presumably, the team moving up from D2 will be pretty upperclassmen-heavy, so you have to good players behind them ready to play at that level.
[2021-05-15 02:36] cdilks : That's why, to use a baseball analogy, I think it's better to just try and hit singles and doubles in recruiting rather than taking home run swings and striking out most years.
[2021-05-15 02:38] naph7777 : Its going to get interesting as the game's overall activity level changes too.
[2021-05-15 02:40] naph7777 : It seems a lot more coaches are picking up 2nd or 3rd teams and there is quite an influx of new users. As things get more competitive, recruiting and promotion is going to get harder. So where previously a consistent building of talent over time used to work, I do wonder if a more uneven recruiting where you team is more cyclic (promoting at the peak of the cycle, barely staying up at the bottom of the cycle) might prove to be the better strategy.

[2021-06-18 01:02] naph7777 : Implications of a hard cap for interest (at Very High): * Any team will know they have an even chance of winning a recruit once they reach Very High. It might take more contacts for an LL6 team to get to Very High than a Legends team, but once you're there you have the same chance. * Landing top talents will be less reliable. Currently if a team in a high league level goes all in on a recruit, there is minimal chance of a lower league level team signing that player. (Both teams might have 135 contacts per season, but the higher team might have 270 "effective contacts" relative to the lower team, so they can outspend them if they want to.) * Teams in general, but particularly at higher levels would likely have larger recruiting boards (can't just sink everything into 1 stud). This will make when/if to offer scholarships a more tactical decision. If you're trying to recruit a big, a shooter and playmaker, you might end up pursuing 2 of each. Do you offer a scholarship to your 2nd choice at a position or not? * It may well be that the interest scale would need to be adjusted so that it took longer to reach Very High, to mitigate some of the above things happening. (I already think this should happen, its not obvious to users who aren't on discord that someone could have spent twice the contacts needed to get to Very High on a recruit and that it makes a difference to their chance of signing the player) * Competition on top recruits probably increases. Maybe good teams end up in multiple lotteries on top tier talent, sometimes they will sign multiple guys in the same year. Some times they'll miss on all of them. * The effects of players signing early or late is greatly reduced. Once you've reached Very High you have the best chance you can get, so you can spend your other contacts elsewhere and know you aren't hurting your chances.
[2021-06-18 01:02] naph7777 : Some of those effects I like, some not so much. It would certainly be different. I don't like the growing sense that I get that signing a top talent will require teams to sink a ridiculous proportion of their recruiting contacts. The implication of that is that the trend will be for the best players to end up on incredibly unbalanced teams (generally bad ones).

His IQ will need to develop to make up for some defensive shortfalls, but he also has the speed to keep quicker guards out of the lane  Moyer could get some minutes next season, but probably benefits more from a RS to fully realize his defensive attributes. He is already a solid shooter but is going to be too small and weak to really take advantage of his post skills. He's more Allen Iverson than Jay Williams with the ball which puts him at SG/SF but prevents him from ever being a true PG  Moyer is more my kind of guy, so give him the slight edge over Masters

[2021-07-05 13:43] eljefe7705 : For everyone who has a 2nd team, what are your thoughts on your 2nd team recruiting players from your 1st team's region? Saw a recruit commit to someone's 2nd team the other day under that scenario, so curious on opinions

[2021-07-05 14:44] tps2.0. : It depends on if both teams were on the guy. I'm fine with someone as long as the two teams were on someone to discourage competition.
[2021-07-05 14:53] slickandjakenillinois : Was there any competition for the out of region player? If not, then there is nothing wrong. If there was, then was the competition a team that their first team is in competition with on another player? If so, then that is an issue. If it is a totally different team that is the competition, then I don’t necessarily have a problem with it.  Is the second team strictly recruiting in the first team’s region? If so that is a problem for me. But if it is a one off because it is a player that could fit on their team, then it is no different than a single team player recruiting out of region. There is not really an advantage for the first team in this scenario.
[2021-07-05 15:04] eljefe7705 : No idea if there were other teams in on the recruit - wasn't someone I was watching
[2021-07-05 15:06] _plokmijn : When I had Penn St I would mostly just stick to in region so I never dealt with any overlap. For Bayamon my goal is to fill my classes with as many in region guys as i can, but bc the Caribbean has such a shallow talent pool I often scout the south for both Bama and Bayamon. My rule is that i’ll never go after a player with interest from a team that is also competing for a recruit with Alabama. It just doesn’t seem fair bc i would have an big contact advantage. Otherwise, I often add no preference to play close to home guys or lower rated prospects from the south as options for Bayamon.

[2021-10-28 02:51] mainecougar : In my limited experience recruiting FR, cap is based on number of contacts spent, not interest level.  Intervals between sub-levels are about what you expect until you have spent 20 or 25 points at which time it takes longer to get to next sub-level than what you would typically expect.  So if you get to low after 2 or 3 points, you can get to high before hitting cap.  But if it takes 4 or more points to get to low, I doubt you will get to high that season. To give you an example, on one FR (in region), it took me 4 (plus scholarship) to get to low and then 7-11-20 to get to med.  I spent 30 and didn't get to med+.  It seems to me that typically you would get to med around 16 or 17 instead of 20 and thus the cap must have come into play.  On another FR, I got to very high in 25 and didn't notice any unusual increase in the intervals to get to the next sub-level.
[2021-10-28 02:55] gards710 : this makes everything make so much sense!!

[2021-12-13 21:45] david118242 : Does anyone try and recruit different types of players, using your backup spot to give you a different option for a specific game plan? Say having one shooting guard that's a lights out shooter and another that is stronger defensively. I'm trying to plan for future classes and wondering if it's worth comparing two players at the same position to try and find something different.
[2021-12-13 21:45] david118242 : I guess usually you may just be trying to get the best player possible and it doesn't work out this way.
[2021-12-13 22:27] cdilks : I wouldn't say I've ever considered it when recruiting, but I did have it work out that way one season with a good scoring SG and a good defensive SG that I switched around based on match-ups and that was successful.
[2021-12-13 22:28] cdilks : The problem is that I think it's tough to have two starter-level guys at the same position at the same time.
[2021-12-13 22:29] cdilks : Ideally, you'd have an upperclassmen starting and then a younger player getting back-up minutes.
[2021-12-13 22:36] bergkamp7349 : I suppose I do try to recruit different kind of players - at least to avoid duplicating a weakness in too many players. If you have 4 big men who get minutes at a time - you don't want more than 2 of them to be slow, you don't want more than 1-2 to be a poor rebounder, you'd like to have 2 at a time who can score inside....if you play 4 guards you want at least 2-3 to have at least some passing to cover PG. If you've got a defensive liability anywhere, you probably don't want to pick up any more in the next couple of classes otherwise you can't cover for them...
[2021-12-13 22:37] naph7777 : Having a team identity that you can game plan to is better than trying to cover everything.
[2021-12-13 22:40] naph7777 : Be a good rebounding, or passing, or shooting team. Have great defence, or be fast/strong, high stamina. Pick something. Then work out the pace, focus and defense settings that highlight your strength.
[2021-12-13 22:42] naph7777 : For example. I picked up more rebounding to cover a weak rebounding C. Now that he’s graduated I’m having a lot more success. Because we win the boards almost every game.
[2021-12-13 22:46] bergkamp7349 : see, Naph is smarter than me - that makes far more sense & probably goes a good way to why I can't get LUPA performing - we don't have an identity. 7 players between 149 and 168 SI and I have mixed up my lineup somewhat, but ultimately finding the one that works best is gonna be the best answer 95% of the time
[2021-12-13 22:49] naph7777 : At lower levels. You can simply out-talent teams. As you go higher talent is generally more equal, if you can’t use the tactics to your advantage (and I’ve had seasons where I felt I couldn’t), then it’s hard to do better than .500
[2021-12-13 22:57] naph7777 : Dunno about being smarter. It’s just something I’ve come back to more recently. I’ve had good SI teams, that weren’t winning as much as I thought they should. Could have just been unlucky, but looking at teams doing better with lower SI, having an identity (or lacking one) seems to be a factor.

[2021-12-27 20:32] slickandjakenillinois : I will give three examples of players on my current team that saw greater growth with lower HS minute years than later higher minute years.  I chose players from my team because they are easily findable, but I have seen numerous other players look similar to this.  My personal belief is that the big jumps, or smaller increases, are more linked to the “error” in the original SI the player has.  The Game manual states a player’s current actual skill may deviate up to 20% from the true value, and the more a player plays the less deviation there is.  I believe the differences most people are seeing is more tied to this deviation versus actual HS minutes played.  But I only have anecdotal evidence such as the three players I am providing here.  Regardless, I haven’t found HS minutes very helpful in projecting player ratings versus other metrics/variables.  But the only way to know for sure is to do a deep dive into the data on a lot of players.  Here are the three examples I give, with Wyatt and Cogswell seeing big jumps freshman year despite low minutes, and Wyatt’s growth slows down the more minutes played.  http://onlinecollegebasketball.org/player/103647/A http://onlinecollegebasketball.org/player/99548/A http://onlinecollegebasketball.org/player/97639/A

[2022-01-02 16:01] slickandjakenillinois : From the game manual:   Scouted Skill Values vs. Real Skill Values  So are the skill values displayed for each player accurate? Just as in real basketball, where there is some uncertainty about a player's talent level, in Hardwood there is also built-in uncertainty in displayed skill levels. The visible skill values for each player are an approximation of his current actual skill level and may deviate by up to 20% from it true value for some skills. Additionally, just like in real basketball, as a player plays more games, his displayed skill value will approach his true current skill level. Note, this may result in a player's displayed skill level actually dropping, even though he is receiving regular coaching and playing time. His skill value is not actually dropping, but because his actual skill level is better known now, a more accurate and lower value is now displayed.

[2022-02-16 20:24] gards710 : yeah, a team certainly doesn't need to be the highest interest level on a recruit (both absolute and relative to other teams) to commit to that team. so a team doesn't need to be at High or Very High, and also a team at Medium can beat a team on High. I believe that High always beats Low, Medium always beats None, and Very High always beats Medium. Some will claim otherwise I'm sure, or claim they were beaten in a case excepting the above.
[2022-02-16 20:26] gards710 : I am not sure that recruits have a set and hidden commit date tbh. I can see it though. Rather, I don't think it is fixed (it's obviously hidden). I think that they have a date but it can change based on things like how many teams/contacts are on them and the difference between the team in the lead and the other teams.
[2022-02-16 20:28] gards710 : what influences a recruit to commit when not at the highest interest? As I understand it from what Steve has said, each team that has invested at least a contact has a certain % of chance to land the player. Each contact carries a weight to it to increase that %. When you invest a certain # of contacts, it reaches a threshold to advance an interest level. That interest level takes into account all of the factors: proximity/location, playing time/depth chart, redshirting, star level, competition from other teams, coach recruiting rating, etc.
[2022-02-16 20:29] gards710 : what happens after the commit's "commit date"? pretty much first come first serve, although the earlier it is in the season, the harder it will be still. Usually won't just be one contact. but it can be

In that case, we are about halfway through the commitment window, so I would start with the assumption that half of the pool has passed their commit date.  Out of the remaining uncommitted players, you would obviously have removed a number of players with a passed date and not removed any with an upcoming date.  So it's safe to assume that more than half of the currently uncommitted players have not reached their commit date yet.  Hard to speculate what that % would be.

[2022-03-01 03:12] cdilks : Yes, as mentioned, it can be tough to tell if you're truly "even" most of the time, since you don't have perfect information on where the other team is at.
[2022-03-01 03:15] cdilks : Also, if I'm not mistaken, even if you're at the same interest level as another team, it means just that. Being in a better division/in-state/etc. makes your contact points worth more and helps you gain interest faster, but those positives in your favor aren't counted for a second time when a player makes a decision.
[2022-03-01 03:15] naph7777 : Its worth noting that the league level factor is already taken into account in raising a recruits interest. If you are both truly equal in interest, then consider it a 50/50 chance. Your edge as a higher team is in how many contacts it will take to get to a certain level of interest.

[2022-06-14 15:34] slickandjakenillinois : I will inject an opinion, or perhaps question, here.  I think the recruiting is very balanced right now.  Sure top tier teams have an advantage, as they should, from their prestige and higher league/division level.  And these top tier players are likely being pursued by one or more top tier teams.  So having top tier teams burn points on top tier players can keep a balance in the recruiting game.  If considering any of these changes, one thing to think about is whether or not it upsets balance, or favors one group of teams over another.  I always found it interesting seeing some managers of top tier teams saying they thought the lower teams have a recruiting advantage (less scholarships, or better prospect for PT, etc.), and lower tier team managers saying the top tier teams have an advantage (less contacts to get interest levels raised, etc.).  That tells me the balance is probably very good.  So do any of these ideas change that balance?  I imagine there will be differing opinions, but fleshing out what some might think could happen, and whether that could impact game balance is always a good thing.

[2022-09-17 02:40] slickandjakenillinois : I understand the frustration, however in my opinion this is one of the balances of the recruiting between established teams and up and coming teams.  Generally the established teams will have some competition because they are on the better players.  If they commit early, or if you know they will commit at a certain time you may have more big teams abandoning the bigger players and going after the “scraps” earlier which would likely be the 3 star players lesser teams are on. It always amazed me when I first started how the established teams thought the recruiting favored the lower division teams and the lower division teams thought recruiting favored the higher division teams.  In actuality they are both right, and both wrong.  There is a balance in the system now and your recruiting strategy needs to change based on where you are at, what your competition is, what level your competition is at, etc.  I love that balance, and not knowing when recruits might commit can help balance the game for the up and coming teams.

[2022-12-13 20:07] bergkamp7349 : the league level largely affects how many points you need to get to the same interest level...so as a lower level team as CFlynn suggested, it's about getting there early on - as you can't outspend a higher team (relatively) later. but smarter on the whole to go for players you feel won't get a lot of competition on them.  specifically, this is from the manual but there's a lot of text in the manual so you may not have seen it "Note: It is very difficult for Division 2 and 3 teams to recruit 4- and 5-star recruits. Division 2 teams will struggle to capture 5-star prospects. Division 3 teams will struggle to attract 4- and 5-star recruits."
[2022-12-13 20:08] bergkamp7349 : but taking over a new team you'll mostly initially be looking at senior prospects anyway - you can tend to gauge by the senior year how much attention they've got

[2022-12-13 20:34] gards710 : Lower level teams can still outspend a higher (d1) team and land a player. It just usually comes at a higher cost, sometimes prohibitive to building the rest of the team
[2022-12-13 20:39] slickandjakenillinois : I will echo Gards here.  D2 and D3 teams have gotten 5 star players, but if they used so many contacts to get them that the rest of the team is lousy, overall the team will also be lousy.  The main goal is to get value out of the contacts you spend in order to get the best team.  If you are in D2 or D3, the main short term goal is to get to D1, therefore 4 and 5 star players are not necessary to achieve this.  Go after players who are decent enough to achieve the short term goal but that you can get at an affordable rate.

Of course, slowly investing allows you to more easily pivot. Pros and cons.

[2023-01-27 13:26] kauffdaddyecsu : There's no "easy" answer, really. Sure, you're a D3 program going against a D1, but prospects (especially those at 3 stars or less) choose D3 teams all the time for various reasons (usually based on roster construction and the possibility of more playing time).
[2023-01-27 13:44] naph7777 : For me this depends more on how many contacts it took you to get to Low interest. How many it did (or will take to get to Low+), and then working out the cost/benefit and risk from there.
[2023-01-27 13:44] slickandjakenillinois : It comes down to how important of a player is he to your team, and do you expect to have to spend so much on him you will sacrifice the overall team, meaning you don’t have enough points to get a supporting cast.
[2023-01-27 13:45] naph7777 : It also depends on the size of your recruiting pool. How many other options do you have? If its a smaller region, do you want to develop a reputation as someone who jumps off a recruit when someone else challenges you? There's potentially more costs in play than just this recruit.
[2023-01-27 13:51] naph7777 : Generally when someone else appears at Low, I want to make sure I have enough contacts to get to at least Medium (preferably High) before I spend another contact. If they get there first and push them higher before me, that may be the info I need to drop that guy. But I want to clearly send the message that I'm all in on this guy, and whoever else is interested should know they need to be the same, or they should look elsewhere.
[2023-01-27 14:12] slickandjakenillinois : Good advice from Naph.  Generally I never challenged for recruits when I thought it would be a costly battle but if I did challenge I had the contacts to stay ahead.  Recently I have gone after recruits and have been greatly challenged on them, sucking my contacts and now leaving me with a relatively empty recruiting board.  So I want to reiterate to make sure you are recruiting a team and not just one player who sucks all your contacts.

[2023-05-21 02:17] furysk : The easiest way to sort out exactly what you need is to look at whats going on in D3.  by pulling all teams in D3 on the rankings page, sort by TI, and then clicking conference, you can see the layout of TPI's per team.  While not all high TPI teams are promoting, usually by the top 6 you have the 3 teams that will promote.  the level has increased a little since back 10 seasons ago, used to be 130 TPI = top 3 or 4 in the conference, but even still the total amongst all 32 conferences that are above 140 TPI are at 45 at seasons end, and likely at around 28 at the start of the season.  that's still just above 9 potential.
[2023-05-21 02:20] furysk : at quick glance, you'll see teams in the top that are starting 124-130 SI bigs.  the best team again probably has 150 SI bigs, but even if you are in conference with him, it's just 1 team that has that.  Ced running Indiana is a good example of a team with only 2 or 3 140+ SI guys that is dominant because it's depth doesn't fall past 115 SI in any position.  So thats why i suggest just getting enough guys of reasonable builds to their cap or there abouts, because in the end you don't need the best.  Ced's doing it with almost all 2 start 10 and 11 potentials (he has two 12's, 1 a 4 and 1 a 3 star,  the rest are lower).

[2023-05-21 05:02] naph7777 : "- Recruiting Calendar The recruiting calendar is broken into 53 updates (one after each game day). At the beginning of the season you'll receive a large sum of recruiting points followed by 2 points for every daily update thereafter. You can use recruiting point to contact a prospect and encourage them to come to your school. Starting with the 5th recruiting update, high school seniors will begin committing to schools. Junior college sophomores and international players will start committing later. On update #53, all uncommitted players will either commit to a school (given a valid scholarship offer), proceed to junior college (and continue to be recruited), become a walk-on at some program or leave basketball altogether."

[2024-02-16 02:59] naph7777 : I think its generally easier to reverse engineer things. Look at teams that are doing well in your teams division (try to find one that has been at that level for a few years and is now likely moving up). Look at the players that are making them successful. Look at their evaluations, what their height/SI was at different years in HS.  From looking at a few of those work out the sort of skills you want to prioritise at different positions. Try and get on recruits that are at a similar level to those teams (who will probably be looking to upgrade what they are looking for in the future).
[2024-02-16 02:59] naph7777 : I mean you can try and work out what is undervalued in the marketplace and succeed with recruits that other people generally don't want.... but that's going to take a lot more experimentation and is generally harder to do.
